data.text:
Agariya Devjibhai vs Union Of India on 10 April, 2024 
Author: Pranay Verma
Bench: Pranay Verma
 1
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore
 BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE PRANAY VERMA  ON THE 10 th OF APRIL, 2024  WRIT PETITION No. 6848 of 2024  BETWEEN:-
 AGARIYA DEVJIBHAI S/O KARSANBHAI OCCUPATION:
 BUSINESS R/O; AGRIYA FLIYU, ANTARJAL, ADIPUR,
 KACHACHH (GUJARAT)
 
 (BY SHRI KULDEEP PATHAK - ADVOCATE)
 AND  1. UNION OF INDIA, SECRETARY MINISTRY OF  COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY PETROLEUM AND  EXPLOSIVE SAFETY ORGANIZATION (PESO) E-7/77  II FLOOR, LALA LAJPAT RAI SOCIETY, NEAR 12  NUMBER BUS STOP, ARERA COLONY, BHOPAL  (MADHYA PRADESH)
 2. STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH, THROUGH  PRINCIPAL SECRETARY DEPARTMENT OF FOOD,
 CIVIL SUPPLIERS AND CONSUMER PROTECTION,
 VALLABH BHAWAN, BHOPAL (MADHYA  PRADESH)
 3. COLLECTOR, DISTRICT - BARWANI (MADHYA  PRADESH)
 4. SUB DIVISIONAL OFFICER (REVENUE) SENDHWA,
 DISTRICT BARWANI (MADHYA PRADESH) 
 .
 (BY SHRI BHUWAN DESHMUKH - GOVERNMENT ADVOCATE)
 This petition coming on for admission this day, th e co  following:
 ORDER By this petition preferred under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, the petitioner has Agariya Devjibhai vs Union Of India on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65218254/
1 challenged the order dated 09.01.2024 passed by the Collector, District Barwani confiscating the vehicle of the petitioner and rejecting his application for grant of custody of the same.
02. The impugned order has been passed under the provisions of Section 6(A) of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 and is an appealable order as per Section 6(C) thereof. Since an alternate and efficacious remedy of preferring an appeal before the appellate authority is available to the petitioner, I do not deem it to be a fit case for invoking extraordinary jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution of India and instead hereby relegate the petitioner to avail the aforesaid remedy of appeal. 
03. In view of the aforesaid, this petition is disposed off with a direction that in case the petitioner prefers an appeal before the appellate authority under Section 6(C) of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 within a period of fifteen days from today, then the appeal shall be decided by the appellate authority on merits in accordance with law within a period of 45 days from the date of filing of the same and shall not be dismissed on the ground of limitation. 
(PRANAY VERMA) JUDGE Shilpa Agariya Devjibhai vs Union Of India on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65218254/
2
